key_insight: Equipping training-free VLN agents with lightweight metacognitive reasoning lets them monitor exploration, detect failure modes (e.g., loops or stalls), and adapt frontier selection, significantly reducing wandering and redundant revisits.
problem_solved: Addresses inefficient exploration in vision-language navigation where greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory cause local oscillation, repeated revisits, and wasted steps—especially in zero-shot, foundation-model-driven agents.
method: Add a metacognitive module that estimates exploration progress and diagnoses failure modes (looping, stalling, low-information frontiers) without extra task-specific training.
Use adaptive frontier selection that deprioritizes recently unproductive regions and prioritizes informative goals inferred from instructions and progress signals.
Maintain an active spatial memory that marks visited/low-value areas and supports replanning and corrective actions to avoid redundant revisits.
impact: Improves efficiency and robustness of zero-shot VLN agents, reducing time, steps, and compute wasted on wandering—making foundation-model-driven navigation more practical for embodied AI and robotics deployments.
visual_elements: Architecture flowchart: Perception -> Metacognitive module (progress estimator + failure detector) -> Adaptive planner -> Action

paper_title: Stop Wandering: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation via Metacognitive Reasoning
paper_authors: Xueying Li, Feng Lyu, Hao Wu, Mingliu Liu, Jia-Nan Liu
